Run a noninteractive source or library-consumer experiment in a disposable
compilation scope. Linux is the initially supported host; other hosts refuse.
No user systemd manager is required.

--output names a new external evidence directory whose parent already exists.
Admitted executions retain invocation.json, result.json, stdout.log and stderr.log.
Setup refusals report their error without claiming execution. --cwd names
the existing source directory. --timeout is a positive budget in seconds,
default 900 and at most 86400. The combined stdout/stderr budget is 64 MiB;
overflow is an explicit failure with the captured prefix retained.

Plumb binds CARGO_TARGET_DIR, PLUMB_HOME and TMPDIR to its newly owned scope.
Existing target bindings and output directories refuse. Captured tool lookup
preserves literal arguments; no shell or environment expansion is introduced.
Inherited inputs are PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ, CARGO_HOME,
RUSTUP_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS.
When an identity is needed, put Runseal in the actual command, for example:

  plumb cache run --output evidence/run-1 --cwd consumer -- runseal :identity.liberte cargo test --locked --offline

The owned process group is stopped before its compilation directory is removed.
Registry and in-directory ownership records must still agree. Unknown process
cleanup or changed ownership preserves material and returns a failure.
Ordinary child status is retained; timeout exits 124, cancellation or a worker
signal exits 128 plus that signal, and unconfirmed cleanup exits 125.

The versioned invocation record names the cwd, literal arguments, owned directory,
registry path, bound tools and timeout. The result records the original child
code/signal, cause and CLI exit. Its process field confirms owned-group settlement
(or that execution never started); directory confirms owned material and registry
removal, and cleanup requires both. Error text is diagnostic, not a stable code.

The in-directory plumb.json and invocation's registry path use
plumb.cache-run-owned/v1: keeper, canonical directory, device and inode must agree.
Treat retained records as evidence; do not rewrite them to obtain cleanup.

Only the created Linux group is supervised. Deliberately escaped groups/sessions
and external services are outside that boundary.

This is not a filesystem sandbox, Guard proof, or Windtun qualification. An
experiment that overrides its target or writes elsewhere owns those outputs.
Forced loss of the supervising Plumb process or host cannot produce a completed
cleanup receipt; retained ownership records remain evidence for explicit recovery.
